To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The von Hippel Lindau (VHL) protein is a tumor suppressor that is inactivated in most clear cell RCCs; 2) The VHL protein acts to target hypoxia-inducing factor (HIF), a key transcription factor in the hypoxia response, for ubiquitination and proteolysis; 3) VHL mutations lead to stabilization of HIF and activation of HIF target genes; 4) HIF is up-regulated

the expression of hypoxia inducible factor (HIF), a transcription factor, is upregulated in most clear cell (cc) renal cell carcinomas and that the pattern is biased toward the expression of the HIF-α isoform 2.

(a) HIF is up-regulated in most clear cell RCCs, but is absent in other renal tumor types; (b) HIF up-regulation is associated with increased angiogenesis and with up-regulation in VEGF expression; (c) HIF up regulation is associated with VHL gene mutations, but also involves other mechanisms; (d) HIF up- regulation is not associated with the presence of pVHL protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel therapeutic approaches in renal cell carcinoma, with particular reference to the role of angiogenesis in this disease.
how cells respond to low oxygen levels and how this process is involved in cancer development.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of renal cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of Hif is not only associated with VHL mutations and upregulation of VEGFA, but is also a marker of the CC-RCC subtype.
HIF activation is a feature of CC-RCC, but that it does not occur in other renal tumors.
the HIF pathway plays an important role in CC-RCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VHL gene is a tumor suppressor gene that is mutated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
HIF-2 is up-regulated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (CC-RCC).
VHL mutations are associated with HIF activation and that HIF activation may be important in the development of renal cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VHL-deficient cells are dependent on HIF-2 for growth and proliferation, and that HIF-2 can be targeted with small molecules to inhibit growth and promote cell death.
HIF-2 is a better target than HIF-1 in RCC.
the HIF pathway plays a role in CC-RCC and is a potential target for therapy.
